h: Divine Kindness Awakens Shame and Opens the Way Back

p: "Though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death,
לֹא אִירָא רָע כִּי אַתָּה עִמָּדִי (תְּהִלִּים כג, ד)
I will fear no evil, for You are with me" (Tehillim 23:4).
In the Midrash (Tanchuma on this parshah, Re'eh 16):
and ours is the shame of face'" (Daniel 9:7);
and it lists there: at the sea,
and likewise after the Giving of the Torah,
the manna came down for them
"and Your manna You did not withhold from their mouth" (Nechemiah 9:20);
and likewise with the idol of Michah;
that the Jew who believes in Hashem
וְרוֹאֶה שֶׁאַף בִּשְׁעַת הַחֵטְא חַס וְשָׁלוֹם
and sees that even at the time of sin, Heaven forbid,
Hashem Yisbarach is with him at that time,
as it says, "Yours, Hashem, is the righteousness"
אָז מִזֶּה יֵשׁ לוֹ בּוֹשֶׁת פָּנִים
then from this he has shame of face
"My God, I am ashamed and blush
to lift up my face to You, my God."
Hashem Yisbarach has mercy on him and saves him.
And this is what they said (Nedarim 20a):
that whoever has no shame of face
it is known that his ancestors did not stand
from the Stand at Mount Sinai:
that the Jew, even at the time of sin,
does not entirely forget Hashem Yisbarach;
and so, when he sees and understands
that even at the time of sin,
אַף עַל פִּי כֵן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ עִמּוֹ
nevertheless Hashem Yisbarach is with him
and watches over him and does good to him
to be ashamed to stand before Hashem Yisbarach
for what we did against His will;
and of itself, through this, one is saved.
וְזֶה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר גַּם כִּי אֵלֵךְ וְגוֹמֵר
And this is what it says: "Though I walk," etc.,
לֹא אִירָא רָע כִּי אַתָּה עִמָּדִי
"I will fear no evil, for You are with me":
that is, from the fact that I see and understand
that even at the time of sin
as it says, "Yours, Hashem, is the righteousness"
from this I have great shame
to lift up my face to You, my God";
every one of Yisrael sees and feels
that Hashem Yisbarach is the one who shepherds him,
and especially at the third meal,
which corresponds to Yaakov Avinu, peace be upon him,
"The God who has shepherded me," etc.;
"Hashem is my shepherd, I shall not want";
that even at the time of sin
and this is "Though I walk," etc.,
And from this comes the shame of face,
and then, of itself, the salvation comes.
And likewise it is expounded in Tanna Devei Eliyahu
that these pesukim refer to Shabbos,
"But to this one will I look,
to the poor and contrite of spirit";
for on Shabbos, when a person sees
from this he becomes poor and contrite of spirit
from all that has passed over him,
and full of shame before Hashem Yisbarach,
"and ours is the shame of face";
it is easy for him to rectify his deeds.
"It is good to give thanks to Hashem"
and it is expounded in Pirkei DeRabbi Eliezer (chapter 19)
"but whoever confesses and forsakes them shall obtain mercy."
And therefore we say this psalm on Shabbos.

inlineHeadings.text: Kindness That Continues Even During Sin
Trust Born From Awareness of Divine Care

paragraphs.text: Source: Nedarim 20a — “… לידי יראת חטא. מיכן אמרו: סימן יפה באדם שהוא ביישן. אחרים אומרים: כל אדם המתבייש, לא במהרה הוא חוטא. ומי שאין לו בושת פנים — בידוע שלא עמדו אבותיו על …” (Oz Vehadar print, p. 54) — “§ It is taught in a baraita: “That His fear may be upon your faces” (Exodus 20:17); this is referring to shame, as shame causes one to blush. “That you not sin” (Exodus 20:17) teaches that shame leads to fear …”
